newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPAIN BOWS OUT AS RENAULT PLANS ROW GROWS.
newsitem.headline: SPAIN BOWS OUT AS RENAULT PLANS ROW GROWS.

text.p: Spain on Friday scrapped attempts to subsidise French carmaker Renault SA's modernisation of a Spanish plant, which the European Union opposed.

"The Spanish government has taken this decision because it doesn't make any sense for Spain that such a small amount of aid...becomes the centre of controversy," an Industry Ministry spokesman told Reuters.

European Commissioner Karel Van Miert threatened on Thursday to block state subsidies to a Renault plant in Valladolid, Spain, saying it was "absurd" for the firm close a profitable plant in Belgium while investing with government aid in Spain.

Spain had asked the European Commission whether it could provide Renault with two billion pesetas, part of the carmakers' 12.5 billion peseta ($13.8 million), plan to modernise and expand the capacity of its plant.
But as outrage grew at Renault's decision last week to close its Vilvoorde, Belgium plant with the loss of 3,100 jobs, Spain scrapped the plan to avoid being engulfed in debate.

It was not clear what impact, if any, Spain's decision would have on Fasa Renault's huge Spanish investment programme. Last year, Fasa-Renault unveiled a plan to invest some 140 billion pesetas in Spain between 1996 and 1999.
The plan envisaged, among other things, hiring another 500 workers for its Valladolid plant to expand production of the Clio model to 1,200 vehicles a day in 1998 from 865.
Labour costs in Spain are 25 percent lower than in Belgium, the company had forecast.

Before Spain's decision, Fasa Renault said it had planned to forge ahead with its plans, shrugging aside the controlversy which has prompted a one-hour union protest strike in Spain, Belgium and France and top level politicial intervention.
But it was not immediately clear if Spain's decision would affect the company's modernisation plan. No comment was available from Renault following the news.
"Fasa Renault will go ahead with planned investments to modernise its plant in Valladolid independent of Brussels' decision," a spokesman for Spanish unit Fasa Renault told Reuters earlier on Friday.
"All our requests for aid were examined with a fine-tooth comb in Brussels and there has never been any problem," the Fasa Renault spokesman said. "Besides it isn't a very significant amount."
Fasa Renault has a work force of more than 12,600. Last year, it lost 4.12 billion pesetas after earning a profit of 1.69 billion pesetas in 1995.
The company has plants in the Spanish cities of Seville and Pelencia in addition to Valladolid.
